content: Before initiating antiretroviral therapy (ART), identify patients from the list of those who may not begin ART shortly after enrolling in HIV care. For the denominator, include patients who started tuberculosis (TB) preventive therapy 12 to 15 months prior to the reporting period, as indicated in the status at enrollment column, and who are not already recorded in the original ART register. Retrieve their HIV patient cards for further review. For the numerator, count the patients from the HIV patient cards who completed TB preventive therapy during the reporting period, as noted in the TB status box on the front of the card. In some settings, a dedicated TB preventive therapy register is available, which significantly simplifies the collection of this indicator. Where such a register exists, count patients who began TB preventive therapy 12 months prior and track whether they completed therapy during the reporting period. The numerator definition has been revised to align with the TB/HIV monitoring and evaluation guidelines. The indicator for early ART initiation in HIV-positive TB patients is defined as the proportion of new and relapsed HIV-positive TB patients who start ART within eight weeks of their TB diagnosis. This indicator is prioritized at national, subnational, and facility levels. The numerator includes the total number of new and relapsed HIV-positive TB patients who started ART within eight weeks of their TB diagnosis, as recorded in the TB register, HIV patient card, or ART register. Relevant data elements include TB status, investigations, ART start date, and visit date. The denominator includes all new and relapsed HIV-positive TB patients identified during the reporting period, with data sourced from the TB register, HIV patient card, or ART register. To collect data for the denominator, identify all patients with confirmed TB (new or relapsed) during the reporting period from the ART register or HIV patient cards. Reconcile this information with the TB register. For the numerator, count patients from the denominator who have an ART start date within eight weeks of their TB diagnosis, as recorded in the ART register or patient card. For profoundly immunosuppressed HIV-positive TB patients, the denominator includes new and relapsed HIV-positive TB patients with a CD4 cell count below 50 cells/mm³ at the time of TB diagnosis. The numerator includes those who started ART within two weeks of their TB diagnosis during the reporting period. This data can be collected during an annual review of patient cards and disaggregated by sex and age (<15 years and 15+ years). Timely initiation of ART is critical to reducing the high fatality rates associated with HIV-related TB. While some indicators may no longer be prioritized, they remain essential for countries that have not yet adopted or are phasing in new guidelines. These indicators may still be relevant for national and subnational reporting. For further guidance, refer to the consolidated guidelines on person-centered HIV patient monitoring and case surveillance, as well as the strategic information guidelines for HIV in the health sector. Additional resources include the WHO guidelines on intensified TB case-finding and isoniazid preventive therapy for people living with HIV, and the 2015 revision of the monitoring and evaluation guide for collaborative TB/HIV activities.
